newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE cocoa erases gains, ends in negative area.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE cocoa erases gains, ends in negative area.

text.p: LIFFE cocoa futures shaved gains in late trading on Tuesday as light origin selling began to creep back into the market.
Lack of selling had allowed prices to perk up on Monday and earlier on Tuesday as traders and speculators covered some shorts.
But sentiment was still bearish on concerns over large supplies from top producer Ivory Coast for a second consecutive season, despite sharply higher European grinds in the third quarter.
"London had a reversal yesterday. That gave a bit of a heart to the upside move. But all we had was another rally off the lows again," said one trader.
The benchmark March contract rose to a session high of 1,010 stg but by the close it had largely trimmed gains and moved to negative territory to stand one stg lower on the day at 1,002 stg a tonne.
Spot month December lost two stg from Monday to 974 stg.
Turnover was an unimpressive 3,873 lots. Traders cited good buying on the Dec/March switch at 28-29 stg while March/May traded at 12-13 stg and Dec/July was at 56 stg.
The market's attention has turned to Ivory Coast where the bareme payment structure for the 1996/97 (October-September) cocoa season is expected to be fixed at the end of this week.
Traders said there was an element of insurance taking by the industry against a possible delay in Ivorian arrivals, but volumes were small.
The third quarter German grind figure is due out on Wednesday or Thursday and may confirm the strong European consumption trend.
The March contract has strong resistance to tackle at 1,025 stg while support is now pegged at around 985 stg.
